_meta.what_this_is: Scores for two systems A and B on the SAME 12 eval cases. Each case has its own difficulty, so scores swing widely from case to case (43 to 95) -- and that case-to-case swing hits A and B together. On every case B beats A by a small, steady margin (2 to 4 points). The question is whether B is really better; the answer depends entirely on whether you compare the two systems case-by-case (paired) or as two separate piles of numbers (unpaired).
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The per-case scores are hand-authored so the between-case variance is large and the per-case A-to-B gap is small and consistent -- exactly the situation where an unpaired test is fooled and a paired test is not. Every statistic is computed in paired.py.
_meta.format: cases: [{case, A, B}] -- A and B are the two systems scored on the same case.
